## Review Submission Flow

Then build and submit with the **file-based flow** (the permission profile denies shell variables, heredocs, and any command that does not start with an allowed prefix — do not attempt them):

**Hex SHA discipline (tools, and why you have them).** LLMs transcribe hex unreliably — a live incident turned `04e61` into `04a61` mid-review and the API rejected the payload. You are given three SHA sources, each for a reason: `/tmp/head_sha.txt` records the commit the workflow checked out for you; the `PR_HEAD_SHA` environment variable carries the same value for quick reference; `git rev-parse HEAD` always tells you what your working tree actually is. They should agree — use whichever is at hand, preferring fresh `git rev-parse` output when in doubt; if they diverge, trust `git rev-parse` and say so. If you deliberately review a different commit than the provided one (e.g., re-verifying against an older base), that is legitimate — write THAT commit's real SHA (from `git rev-parse <commit>`, not from memory) in your footer and marker, and say in the summary which commit you reviewed and why.

1. Read the SHA file and record its value: `cat /tmp/head_sha.txt`
2. Write the comments you placed for inline delivery as a JSON array to `/tmp/review_comments.json` using your file tools (same object shape as the scratchpad: `path`, `line`, optional `start_line`, `side`, `body`). Use `[]` if none earned inline placement.
3. Write your summary to `/tmp/review_body.md` using your file tools. Write your own, human-feeling summary — don't copy templates verbatim. Structure: verdict line, then the summary shape YOUR protocol section defines (FIRST: Overall Assessment; FOLLOW-UP: Previous feedback - status, Assessment of New Changes, Overall Status), with your findings grouped under the severity headings (`### 🔴 Critical`, `### 🟠 Major`, `### 🟡 Minor`, `### 🔵 Info` — omit empty groups; each entry `file:line — one-line description`), plus **Questions for the Author** on FIRST reviews (omit when self-reviewing). End the body with BOTH footer lines, written by you using the value you read in step 1 (this declares what commit you actually reviewed):
```
_This review was generated by an AI assistant._
<!-- last_reviewed_sha:<the value from /tmp/head_sha.txt> -->
```
4. Validate both inputs — each command must exit 0 before you continue (a failure IS the gate; the agent shell has no stdin, hence `-n`):
```bash
jq -e 'type == "array"' /tmp/review_comments.json
```
```bash
jq -n -e --rawfile body /tmp/review_body.md --rawfile sha /tmp/head_sha.txt '($body | test("<!-- last_reviewed_sha:" + ($sha | rtrimstr("\n")) + " -->"))'
```
The first fails loudly if the comments file is not a JSON array (e.g. accidental JSONL — `--slurpfile` would otherwise silently submit only the first object). The second fails loudly if the marker you wrote does not byte-match the SHA file — normally that means a transcription error. The one legitimate exception: if you deliberately reviewed a different commit than the file's, your marker will not match by design — verify it against THAT commit's real `git rev-parse` output instead, state the divergence in your summary, and proceed; the workflow's post-verification preserves resolvable declarations.
5. Combine and sanity-check:
```bash
jq -n --rawfile body /tmp/review_body.md --rawfile sha /tmp/head_sha.txt --slurpfile comments /tmp/review_comments.json '{event: "COMMENT", commit_id: ($sha | rtrimstr("\n")), body: $body, comments: $comments[0]}' > /tmp/review_payload.json
```
```bash
jq -c '.comments | length' /tmp/review_payload.json
```
6. Submit:
```bash
gh api --method POST -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR_NUMBER}/reviews" --input /tmp/review_payload.json
```
Replace `"COMMENT"` in step 5 with the event you chose. Both step-4 checks must exit 0 before combining. The workflow verifies the posted footers afterwards and repairs them if needed, but a mismatch means your declared reviewed-commit is wrong — fix it yourself before submitting.

For self-reviews, use the humorous body shape from the Self-Review Tone section of this prompt (Self-Review Assessment / Architectural Reflections / Key Fixes I Should Make), but keep the SAME canonical footer lines above — the workflow's footer verification expects exactly this signature regardless of review tone.
